A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PersonaX datasets and causal representation learning framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM-selection and prompt-consistency experiments, statistical dependence analyses, synthetic representation-learning results, and real-data causal graphs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds MMCRL causal-graph results on both PersonaX datasets in Appendix A9.3.

M1.justification: The trait-generation and aggregation procedures, multimodal multi-measurement CRL architecture, and reconstruction, independence, and sparsity objectives remain unchanged. Appendix A9.3 evaluates an existing baseline without modifying the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CelebPersona's 9,444 public figures, AthlePersona's 4,181 male athletes across seven leagues, and the same colored-MNIST/Fashion-MNIST synthetic task. The added baseline analysis uses the existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: MMCRL, already a synthetic comparator in v1, is newly evaluated in the real-data comparisons in A9.3. The synthetic comparator set remains BetaVAE, MCL, and MMCRL. Table 1 also relabels Qwen-Plus as QwQ-32B with identical scores; QwQ-32B was already listed in v1's Table A5.

E3.justification: The reported sampling, prompt scales, evaluation metrics, significance threshold, and Table A7 training settings remain unchanged. The added MMCRL comparison follows the existing real-data analysis setup and specifies no distinct new split, metric, or testing procedure.

E4.justification: A9.3 extends the real-data graph case studies with comparisons of graph density, interpretability, and separation between visual and behavioral factors against MMCRL. Existing prompt-sensitivity and RCIT analyses are retained; no new stability or robustness test accompanies the comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 trials per prompt format and standard deviations in A4.2, alongside the same independence-test significance reporting. The added MMCRL analysis introduces no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical comparison procedure.

E6.justification: Figures A8–A9 add MMCRL causal graphs for CelebPersona and AthlePersona, with new qualitative comparative findings. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including synthetic R²/MCC scores of 0.96/0.92 for the proposed method and 0.90/0.85 for MMCRL.

T1.justification: A6.1 locally corrects the proof's uniqueness argument to invoke Assumption iii instead of Assumption 4 and changes the conditioning variable to estimated w in v2 Equation 28, corresponding to v1 Equation 30. The theorem statements and substantive assumptions remain unchanged; most other proof edits simplify wording and equation presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: two multimodal datasets, structured dependence analysis, and a multimodal multi-measurement CRL framework with identifiability guarantees. The added baseline evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: A9.3 newly argues that multi-measurement modeling yields sparser, more stable, and more semantically coherent real-data graphs than single-measurement MMCRL. These interpretations are qualitative. Existing cohort restrictions, temporal limitations, and ethical discussions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer in the abstract and specifies that the new MMCRL analysis uses the hyperparameters in Table A7. Existing architecture details, embedding dimensions, prompt templates, and hyperparameter values are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works, including Hu and Schennach on nonclassical measurement error and recent work on causal learning and reflective reasoning. A6.1 explicitly connects its operator argument to nonparametric identification literature. These are limited contextual additions without a broad repositioning.

P1.justification: v2 edits the prose of the first theorem's proof, makes smaller main-text wording changes, expands the LLM-model listing, and adds subsection A9.3. Publication headers, an author affiliation, and acknowledgments also change. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two baseline graph diagrams, Figures A8–A9, adjusts Table 1's labels and column spacing, and reflows appendix material such as Prompt 2 and Figure A7. The contents of the retained figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added real-data MMCRL graphs provide a useful comparison missing from v1, while local proof corrections and the code pointer improve clarity and reproducibility information. The gains are limited: A9.3's interpretability and stability arguments remain qualitative, with no new real-data quantitative validation or uncertainty analysis.
